description: Which v1.10.0 cluster definitions and locks a reader MUST accept or reject. A definition is accepted if it parses under the field rules (fixed lengths, addresses, deposit amount bounds and sum) and its stored hashes match. A lock is accepted if it parses and passes the full verification sequence: hashes, public shares, deposit data, builder registrations, signature aggregate, node signatures (against node_pubkeys). Every rejected case breaks exactly one rule and is otherwise fully valid; length and address cases are hashed and signed over the value a lenient reader would decode (short fields left-padded as Charon pads them, the registration fee recipient right-padded, long fields truncated, addresses case-insensitive), so a reader that pads instead of rejecting finds every hash and signature valid.

provenance.note: Built by this spec: the rules are stricter than charon at this ref, which parses most rejected cases (and verifies their hashes and signatures) without complaint. Keys are reused from bls_threshold.json and the real_keys_3_of_4 lock in cluster_hashing.json. This script fails if the spec's verdict or reason differs from the one a case was built for.

definition.name: checksummed_addresses
definition.notes: The valid base definition: an unsigned definition as `charon create cluster` writes it, with absent (empty) operator and creator addresses and signatures, and EIP-55 checksummed validator addresses.

definition.name: lowercase_addresses
definition.notes: All-lowercase addresses carry no checksum and are accepted as written.

definition.name: uppercase_addresses
definition.notes: All-uppercase hex digits (with a lower-case 0x) carry no checksum either.

definition.name: signed_operators
definition.notes: Operator and creator addresses and 65-byte signatures present. The signatures are placeholders: only their lengths are in scope here.

definition.name: zero_addresses_on_testnet
definition.notes: The zero address is a valid validator address.

definition.name: deposit_amounts_at_standard_bounds
definition.notes: 1 ETH and 32 ETH, the bounds for 0x01 credentials.

definition.name: deposit_amounts_sum_to_exactly_32_eth
definition.notes: 16 ETH twice: repetition is allowed, and 32 ETH is the smallest valid sum.

definition.name: deposit_amounts_sum_one_gwei_below_32_eth
definition.notes: 16 ETH and 16 ETH less one Gwei: each amount is in range but they sum to one Gwei under 32 ETH, as Charon's VerifyDepositAmounts rejects.

definition.name: single_deposit_amount_below_32_eth_total
definition.notes: A single 1 ETH amount: in range, but non-empty amounts must sum to at least 32 ETH.

definition.name: deposit_amounts_at_compounding_bounds
definition.notes: 1 ETH and 2048 ETH with compounding set.

definition.name: bad_withdrawal_address_checksum
definition.notes: Mixed case with one letter's case flipped. The hashes are those of the correctly spelled address, which is what a case-insensitive reader decodes, so only the checksum check rejects it.

definition.name: bad_fee_recipient_checksum
definition.notes: As bad_withdrawal_address_checksum, for the fee recipient.

definition.name: address_without_0x_prefix
definition.notes: 40 hex digits with no 0x. The hashes are of the prefixed address.

definition.name: empty_withdrawal_address
definition.notes: A validator address is never absent. Charon hashes an empty address as the zero address, and the hashes here are computed that way.

definition.name: withdrawal_address_19_bytes
definition.notes: One byte short. The hashes are of the address left-padded to 20 bytes.

definition.name: zero_withdrawal_address_on_mainnet
definition.notes: The zero address is valid on mainnet too. Charon's create dkg refuses it as policy, but deployed mainnet clusters use it deliberately, so a reader must accept it.

definition.name: zero_fee_recipient_on_mainnet
definition.notes: A zero fee recipient on mainnet is valid as well.

definition.name: zero_withdrawal_address_on_gnosis
definition.notes: And on Gnosis Chain (fork version 0x00000064).

definition.name: deposit_amount_below_1_eth
definition.notes: 999999999 Gwei, one Gwei under the minimum.

definition.name: deposit_amount_above_32_eth_without_compounding
definition.notes: 32 ETH plus one Gwei with 0x01 credentials.

definition.name: deposit_amount_above_2048_eth_with_compounding
definition.notes: 2048 ETH plus one Gwei with compounding set.

definition.name: fork_version_3_bytes
definition.notes: Charon left-pads a short fixed-size field, so the hashes are those of 0x00 followed by these three bytes.

definition.name: operator_config_signature_64_bytes
definition.notes: A signature one byte short. The hashes are of it left-padded to 65 bytes, as Charon pads it.

lock.name: valid_lock
lock.notes: The valid base lock: one validator with the bls_threshold.json sharing, one 32 ETH deposit and a builder registration signed by the group key, a real signature aggregate and real node signatures.

lock.name: default_deposit_amounts
lock.notes: deposit_amounts is empty, so the deposits are Charon's defaults for 0x01 credentials: 1 ETH and 32 ETH.

lock.name: compounding_deposits
lock.notes: compounding is set, so the credentials take the 0x02 prefix and a single deposit may carry up to 2048 ETH.

lock.name: default_compounding_deposit_amounts
lock.notes: Compounding with empty deposit_amounts: Charon's defaults are 1, 8, 32 and 256 ETH.

lock.name: withdrawal_credentials_bare_address
lock.notes: The 20-byte withdrawal address with no prefix or padding. Left-padded, as Charon pads it, this becomes 0x00-prefixed (BLS) credentials; the lock hash and deposit signature are over that padded value, so every signature verifies for a reader that pads.

lock.name: withdrawal_credentials_31_bytes
lock.notes: The credentials without their prefix byte. Left-padding restores a 0x00 prefix, which is what the hashes and signatures are over.

lock.name: withdrawal_credentials_33_bytes
lock.notes: Valid credentials with one byte appended. The hashes and signatures are of the valid 32 bytes, which is what a reader that truncates sees.

lock.name: withdrawal_credentials_0x00_prefix
lock.notes: Correct length, BLS (0x00) prefix, signed as carried.

lock.name: withdrawal_credentials_0x02_prefix_without_compounding
lock.notes: 0x02 credentials in a definition that does not set compounding.

lock.name: withdrawal_credentials_0x01_prefix_with_compounding
lock.notes: 0x01 credentials in a compounding definition.

lock.name: withdrawal_credentials_nonzero_padding
lock.notes: Correct prefix and address with a non-zero byte in the eleven padding bytes.

lock.name: withdrawal_credentials_for_another_address
lock.notes: Well-formed credentials for an address the definition does not name.

lock.name: deposit_pubkey_is_not_the_group_key
lock.notes: The deposit names the first public share and is validly signed by that share's secret.

lock.name: deposit_amount_not_in_definition
lock.notes: A validly signed 16 ETH deposit against deposit_amounts of 32 ETH.

lock.name: deposit_amount_not_in_default_amounts
lock.notes: deposit_amounts is empty, so only Charon's defaults are allowed; 16 ETH is not one of them.

lock.name: bad_deposit_signature
lock.notes: The deposit carries 32 ETH but its signature is over the same message with 31 ETH.

lock.name: deposit_signed_for_another_network
lock.notes: Signed with the mainnet deposit domain in a Hoodi cluster. The deposit domain is computed from the definition's fork_version.

lock.name: deposit_signature_95_bytes
lock.notes: A BLS signature one byte short. The lock hash is over it left-padded, so the lock hash, aggregate and node signatures verify for a reader that pads; the padded deposit signature itself does not.

lock.name: pubshare_47_bytes
lock.notes: A public share one byte short. The lock hash is over it left-padded.

lock.name: registration_fee_recipient_19_bytes
lock.notes: Charon hashes this field right-padded, unlike every other fixed field, so the lock hash and registration signature are over the address with its last byte zeroed and the file carries it with that byte dropped.

lock.name: registration_fee_recipient_not_in_definition
lock.notes: The registration names another fee recipient and is validly signed over it.

lock.name: registration_signed_for_definition_fee_recipient
lock.notes: The registration names another fee recipient but its signature is over the definition's. Charon verifies the signature over a message rebuilt from the definition and accepts this; the spec compares the carried message first.

lock.name: registration_pubkey_is_not_the_group_key
lock.notes: The registration message names the first public share.

lock.name: bad_registration_signature
lock.notes: The registration's signature is over a different gas limit.

lock.name: bad_address_checksum_in_lock
lock.notes: The address rules apply to the definition inside a lock too. Hashes and signatures are over the correctly spelled address.

lock.name: zero_withdrawal_address_on_mainnet_lock
lock.notes: A fully signed mainnet lock whose deposit credentials are derived from the zero withdrawal address. Valid: such locks exist on mainnet by design.
